_meta: Lead-chasing follow-up round after AF/G.23, 2026-08-13. Targets the single open lead ga-g23-municipal.json left on the Fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales (dropped there as reason 'deferred': 'no 2021-2026 primary document confirms whether the fund is currently operational'). Outcome is a genuinely MIXED answer, not a clean resolution: the FY2025 Loi de Finances now carries a real, code-bearing 'Péréquation Collectivités' budget line (402,261,680 FCFA, +9% vs LFI 2024) and a June 2026 ministerial statement on the official gouvernement.ga portal says the fund 'a été mis en place' (has been established) — but its funding sources are still described in the conditional ('devrait être alimenté'), and NEITHER the Cour des Comptes' 2022 RELF (already in corpus) NOR its newer 2023 RELF isolates péréquation-specific execution from the aggregate 'collectivités locales' transfer line, so disbursement-to-communes remains unconfirmed by any primary document. A July 2026 claim of 'inopérabilité prolongée' is SECONDARY-ONLY (two Gabonese news outlets, sourced to an unnamed internal compte rendu not found on gouvernement.ga) and directly contradicts the June 2026 primary statement — recorded as a note, not resolved into an edge, since it cannot itself support one and the tension is left standing rather than adjudicated. Net effect on the AF/G.23 lead: upgraded from 'no document at all' to 'a funded line exists, execution unconfirmed, and a live secondary dispute over operability is unresolved' — the honest state of the evidence, not a tidy yes/no.

reports.title: Loi de Finances 2025 — ligne budgétaire 712 "Péréquation Collectivités" (Article 21)
reports.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise / Présidence de la République
reports.description: Gabon's FY2025 Finance Law, published in the Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise (66e année, N°51 Bis Spécial, 20 janvier 2025). Article 21, p.31 (Chapitre 4), sets prélèvements au profit des collectivités locales for 2025 at 29,058,048,393 FCFA and itemises them by line code, including: "712 | Péréquation Collectivités | 369 385 095 [LFI 2024] | 402 261 680 [LF 2025] | 32 876 585 [écart] | 9% [écart %]" — i.e. a named, code-bearing 'Péréquation Collectivités' beneficiary funded at 402,261,680 FCFA for 2025, up 9% from 369,385,095 FCFA in LFI 2024. This confirms the fund named in Articles 250-252 of the 2014/2015 organic decentralization law now has a real annual appropriation, not merely a paper statute. CAVEATS: (1) accessed via a third-party mirror (directinfosgabon.com), not the .gouv.ga domain directly, because journal-officiel.ga's own search interface is non-functional/JS-rendered and returned no result for this instrument this round; the PDF's own masthead unambiguously identifies it as the official Journal Officiel, so the document itself is treated as primary despite the indirect access route. (2) An appropriation is not the same fact as a disbursement: no Cour des Comptes execution report (2022 or 2023 edition) isolates péréquation-specific spending from the aggregate 'collectivités locales' transfer total, so whether this line was actually paid out to communes in 2025 is NOT confirmed by any primary document located this round — see ga-courcomptes-relf-2022 and the _dropped RELF 2023 entry in this file. (3) A June 2026 ministerial statement (Interior Minister Adrien Nguema Mba, via gouvernement.ga) separately confirms the fund 'a été mis en place' (has been established) but describes its funding sources — a share of state own-revenue plus oil/forestry/mining-sector resources — only in the conditional ('devrait être alimenté'), suggesting the funding mechanism was still being finalised as of that date even though this FY2025 line already exists. (4) A July 2026 secondary-only report (two Gabonese news outlets, not government-authored, sourced to an unnamed internal compte rendu not locatable on gouvernement.ga) claims an interministerial committee found the fund's 'inopérabilité prolongée' (prolonged non-operability) as of July 23, 2026, directly contradicting the June 2026 ministerial claim; this is recorded here as an unresolved tension in the evidence, not adjudicated either way.
reports.cadence_note: One-off annual budget-law entry for FY2025; the enclosing Loi de Finances itself recurs annually but no cadence is asserted for this specific line item's continuation or amount.

dependencies.basis: The organic decentralization law's Article 250 institutes the 'fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales' and Article 252 states it is funded by 'un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances' — i.e. the organic law itself designates the annual Finance Law as the instrument that sets the fund's actual take rate/amount each year. The FY2025 Finance Law's Article 21 line item 712 ('Péréquation Collectivités', 402,261,680 FCFA) is exactly that designated annual act: it is not merely citing the fund for context, it is the yearly mechanism Article 252 names as the fund's funding source, applied. That is a genuine data/figure dependency (the budget line's existence and legal basis flow from Article 252's designation) rather than a loose contextual reference, so uses_data_from is chosen over cites. Not calculated_from, since the 402,261,680 FCFA figure is not itself derived by a stated formula from anything in the organic law — the organic law sets the mechanism (that a rate is fixed annually in the finance law), not the rate itself.
dependencies.evidence_quote: un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances

_dropped.why: Checked the Cour des Comptes' newer RELF 2023 edition (https://courcomptes.ga/download/84/publications/13977/relf_2023.pdf, 'Rapport d'exécution de la loi de finances 2023') for a péréquation-specific execution figure that would confirm disbursement of the budget line to communes. Full-text search for 'péréquation' returns zero matches, exactly as in the 2022 edition already in corpus (ga-courcomptes-relf-2022). The report does contain a 'Gestion des collectivités locales' program-level breakdown (Titre 4 transfers): prévision 16,441,782,998 FCFA vs. exécution 9,990,013,178 FCFA (~60.77%), but this is an aggregate figure covering all local-government transfers, not péréquation isolated from the rest. Also checked and negative: the Cour des Comptes' Rapport de Certification des Comptes de l'État, Exercice 2024 (Sept 2025, https://courcomptes.ga/download/84/publications/13978/rcce_2024.pdf) — no péréquation mention found. No primary document located this round isolates péréquation-specific execution/disbursement from aggregate local-government transfer figures, in any year checked (2022 or 2023 RELF, or the 2024 certification report).

Two Gabonese news outlets (gabonreview.com and lunion.ga/sonapresse), neither primary/government-authored, reported around July 24-26, 2026 that an interministerial committee meeting on July 23, 2026, presided by Vice-President Hermann Immongault, found 'l'inopérabilité prolongée du Fonds national de péréquation' (prolonged non-operability), reportedly sourced to an unnamed 'compte rendu de la Vice-présidence du gouvernement,' with resources to be formally inscribed in the 2027 Loi de Finances. This directly contradicts the June 2026 ministerial statement quoted in ga-loi-finances-2025-perequation-ligne's description ('a été mis en place'). The primary compte rendu itself was searched for on gouvernement.ga (browsed the Conseil interministériel archive and ran the site's own search for 'péréquation' and 'comité interministériel décentralisation') and not found — the site's July 2026 news archive has no entry between July 6 and August 2, 2026, so either this meeting's compte rendu was never published there or falls in an archive gap. Recorded as 'note' rather than 'caveat' because there is no live edge for this to annotate (a caveat's source/target must name a real minted edge, and this claim, being secondary-only and unconfirmed, does not support minting one) and rather than 'resolved' because nothing here was resolved — the tension between the June 2026 primary statement and this July 2026 secondary claim is left standing, not adjudicated.

Attempted to check the Interior/Decentralisation ministry's own decentralisation.gouv.ga subdomain for pages on the Fonds de péréquation's operational status (e.g. FEICOM-style cohésion-des-territoires or fund-management pages) that might help resolve the tension between the June 2026 'established' statement and the July 2026 'non-operability' claim. The domain's TLS certificate is self-signed, blocking a normal fetch/verification and preventing any content from being read this round. Flagged as a blocked lead for a future round with tooling that can accept or bypass the certificate safely.

Flagged for a future round to re-check once/if the site's search is fixed.
